solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dame fills gap in market restoring rare vehicle

indicators.note: restoring is read as re-storing, putting the assembled letters back the other way round
fills says the dame's name goes into the space left in the market word
a gap in the word market leaves only its outside letters, the middle being emptied

parts.note: Dame Edna Everage, the comic stage character, gives the name Edna

explanation.surface: A grand lady plugs a hole in the market by refurbishing an unusual old vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gap in market' leaves MT; 'fills' puts EDNA inside to give MEDNAT, which 'restoring' turns round. Dame Edna Everage is Barry Humphries' comic stage character.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle built for two riders is an uncommon sight, so a rare vehicle describes it.

clue.text: Detest Hobart's traffic (Tasmania's capital to be avoided)

indicators.note: traffic, as in to trade or deal in, here means the letters are dealt out afresh in a new order
to be avoided says the named letter is taken out of the city's name

parts.note: Hobart is the capital city of Tasmania; the possessive adds no letter

indicators.note: the capital of the word Tasmania is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone hates the traffic in Hobart and wants to steer clear of Tasmania's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tasmania's capital' looks like Hobart again, but it is just T; removing it from HOBART leaves HOBAR, which 'traffic' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something intensely is a direct synonym for detesting it.

clue.text: Appoint gent with ideas, at work

indicators.note: at work suggests the letters are busy, being worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A boss picks a man with good ideas for a post at the office.
explanation.definitionFit: To name someone officially to a position is the verb's usual meaning, a straight synonym for appoint.

clue.text: He wrote notes, outwardly hysterical, filling paper when uplifted

indicators.note: filling says the outside letters go inside the turned paper word
in a down clue, uplifted means the paper word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, five hundred sheets

indicators.note: outwardly takes just the outside letters of the word hysterical

explanation.surface: Someone writing frantic notes, wild on the outside, stuffing a lifted stack of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when uplifted' turns REAM to MAER; 'outwardly hysterical' gives HL, which goes in the middle. 'Notes' are musical ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Mahler was an Austrian composer of symphonies, so he literally wrote musical notes.

clue.text: Explorer retired in final leg — America

indicators.note: retired says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An explorer retires during the last stage of a journey to America.
explanation.walkthrough: The run fiNAL LEG AMerica, read in reverse, spells the name; 'retired' means withdrew, going back. 'in' marks the letters as sitting inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand Magellan was the Portuguese navigator whose expedition first circled the globe.

clue.text: Novelist spread books amongst real fans after trade declined

indicators.note: after says the crowd of people comes behind the rearranged trade

parts.note: marg is short for margarine, a bread spread

indicators.note: declined, as in gone downhill, means the letters of trade fall into disorder
amongst puts the books letters inside the rearranged word
fans, as in spreads out, means the letters of real are fanned into a new order

parts.note: B is book, so BB stands for books

explanation.surface: A business that spread books among keen readers after trade fell off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declined' rearranges TRADE to ARETD; 'fans' rearranges REAL around BB to give RABBLE. Marg is a British shortening of margarine.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Drabble is an English writer of novels such as The Millstone.

clue.text: Illumination minor after element twisted

indicators.note: after says the minor word follows the element
twisted means the element symbol is turned round

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, an element
slight means minor or insignificant

explanation.surface: A small light produced after some chemical element is twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'element' tempts GAS, but the element is silver, Ag, which 'twisted' turns to GA.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from burning coal gas was the standard street and home illumination before electricity.

clue.text: Slug you finally left climbing flower

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the pieces are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a slug of drink is a nip, a small measure

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A garden slug that you finally left climbing a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slug' is a drink, not the garden pest. NIP, U and L read upwards make the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a tall garden plant with spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: Naked son exits steam bath with disastrous result (extremity of his neglected)

indicators.note: exits says the son letter leaves the steam bath word

parts.note: a sauna is a steam bath

indicators.note: disastrous suggests a mess, so the remaining letters are jumbled
neglected says that letter is left out of the word result
the extremity of his is its final letter

explanation.surface: A naked son leaves the sauna, with disastrous consequences, his privates neglected.
explanation.walkthrough: SAUNA less S gives AUNA. 'extremity of his' is S; 'neglected' drops it from RESULT, and 'disastrous' rearranges RELUT to TUREL.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means in the natural state, used in English for being unclothed.

clue.text: New shop repeatedly attracts right posh element

indicators.note: attracts says the right and posh letters are drawn inside
repeatedly says the rearranged word occurs twice
new means the letters of shop are made over into a new arrangement

parts.note: U means upper class, hence posh

explanation.surface: A new shop keeps drawing in the right posh customers.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOP rearranged twice gives PHOS PHOS, and R and U go into the second, before its last letter. U for upper class is an old British term.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosphorus is a chemical element, number 15, that glows in the dark.

clue.text: Writer's agent follows positive tone

indicators.note: follows says the writer's agent comes after positive

parts.note: ink is the agent or medium a writer uses

explanation.surface: A literary agent takes up an upbeat tone with a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's agent' suggests a literary representative; it is the stuff a pen writes with.
explanation.definitionFit: A tone can be a shade of colour, and pink is one such shade.

clue.text: Heard dog barking somewhere in Ireland

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters are deranged

explanation.surface: Someone heard a dog barking somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' seems to describe the dog, but it means crazy and rearranges HEARD DOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Drogheda is a town in County Louth on the River Boyne, a place in Ireland.

clue.text: Congenital convict, back in prison for months

indicators.note: for says one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: an inmate is a convict held in jail

indicators.note: back in takes the last letter of prison

explanation.surface: A born criminal, back in prison for some months.
explanation.walkthrough: The back of 'prison', N, replaces M (months) in INMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something congenital is present from birth, inborn, which is what innate means.

clue.text: Rhyming scheme created by pop group?

definitions.meaning: a verse pattern where the outer lines rhyme together and the inner two rhyme together
the Swedish band that won Eurovision with Waterloo

explanation.surface: A rhyming pattern produced by a band.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters label an enclosed rhyme pattern and also name the famous Swedish quartet.

clue.text: Swelling, to face, formed eating hospital meat

parts.note: a boil is an inflamed swelling on the skin

indicators.note: to face is to turn round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
eating says the formed word takes in the hospital letter

parts.note: made means formed

explanation.surface: A swelling on the face developed, needing a hospital visit.
explanation.walkthrough: MADE eats H to give MAHDE, which 'to face' turns round to EDHAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham cooked in water is a common cold cut, a cooked meat.

clue.text: Training converted border starts to eliminate rodent and insect

indicators.note: converted means the training letters are changed round

parts.note: PE is physical education, training
a hem is a border on fabric

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Training in how to deal with a border, starting with getting rid of rodents and insects.
explanation.definitionFit: The mayfly, whose adult life lasts a day, belongs to the insect order named Ephemera.

clue.text: Order chap to leave vegetable?

parts.note: read as a command to a man to clear off, the words sound like a French-named pea eaten pod and all

explanation.surface: Someone orders a chap to leave the vegetable patch.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into French-ish words, the vegetable's name reads like 'Man, get out!', an order to a chap to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugar pea, eaten pod and all, is a garden vegetable whose French name means eat-all.

clue.text: Sweet, alcoholic purchases keep party swinging

indicators.note: swinging means swung round, so the whole is read upwards
keep says the purchases word holds the party word

parts.note: buys means purchases
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: Alcoholic purchases keep a party going in swinging style.
explanation.walkthrough: BUYS around BALL gives BUBALLYS, which 'swinging' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: This old English dessert is whipped cream with wine or sherry, a boozy pudding.

clue.text: Naive group of women extremely easily bound by document

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation

indicators.note: bound by says the extreme letters are enclosed within the document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document

indicators.note: extremely takes the outer letters of easily

explanation.surface: A naive group of women is easily bound by a legal document.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British countrywomen's organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being innocently amazed by everything shows the gullibility of someone naive.

clue.text: Poles welcome the Italian and Swede perhaps

indicators.note: welcome says the poles take in the Italian article

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: Polish people welcome an Italian and a Swede.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the nationality but means the north and south poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Nils is a common Scandinavian boy's name, so a Swede might be called it.

clue.text: Times article probes FA rejecting player from Africa?

indicators.note: probes says the times and article letters push inside
rejecting turns the nothing word back on itself

parts.note: sweet FA means nothing, nil
by means times, as in multiplied by
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Times article examines the Football Association turning down an African player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'FA' seems the Football Association; 'sweet FA' is British slang for nothing, NIL, reversed to LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer from Libya is a player from that North African country.

clue.text: Grant requires particular envelope to return prickly plant

indicators.note: to return means the whole is sent back, reversed
requires says the grant word needs the envelope inside it

parts.note: let means grant or allow
an SAE is a stamped addressed envelope, a particular kind

explanation.surface: A grant application requires a specific envelope for its return.
explanation.walkthrough: LET with SAE inside makes LESAET, which 'to return' turns round. SAE is a British abbreviation for a stamped addressed envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The teasel is a thistle-like plant with spiny flower heads once used to comb cloth.

clue.text: River bends back bush

indicators.note: back means the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: the Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge
U-bends, so bends gives the plural of U

explanation.surface: A river bends back around a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam is the river of Cambridge; 'bends' is U-bends, Us.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree with red autumn leaves and spice berries.

clue.text: Flipping bond 'experts' emptied investment fund, in my opinion

indicators.note: flipping says the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a tie is a bond

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside of experts, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: an ISA is an individual savings account, a British tax-free fund

explanation.surface: Bond experts drained an investment fund, frankly a flipping disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive but turns the pieces round. An ISA is a British tax-free savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase prefaces a personal view, an idiom meaning from my point of view.

clue.text: Woman that is holding wingless little bird

indicators.note: holding says the that-is letters enclose the clipped bird

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: wingless clips a wing, an end letter, off the bird

parts.note: the wren is a tiny bird

explanation.surface: A woman holding an injured little bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female first name, so it fits woman.

clue.text: Copper's intertwined with royal associate

indicators.note: intertwined says the letters of the two pieces are woven together

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
HM is His or Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A policeman is closely linked with a member of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal; its letters weave alternately with HM.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal or friend is a close associate.

clue.text: Sportsman keeps 'orse and stable, primarily for US teenager

indicators.note: keeps says the sportsman holds the horse and stable letters

parts.note: a boxer is a sportsman
a hobby is a small horse; drop the H as in 'orse

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of stable

explanation.surface: A sportsman keeps a horse and a stable, mainly for an American teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orse drops the H to signal hobby (a small horse) losing its H too. 'and' simply joins the two inserted pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobbysoxers were 1940s American teenage girls in ankle socks, fans of crooners.

clue.text: 1760 yards occupied by public transport — like a no. 25?

indicators.note: occupied by says the distance phrase has the transport sitting inside it

parts.note: 1760 yards make up a single mile
a cab or taxi is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A mile of road taken up by public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: A MILE takes CAB inside, between MI and LE. No. 25 is CHUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Being friendly and on good terms is how a pal behaves.

clue.text: Spice girl fan previously

indicators.note: previously says the fan word comes before the girl

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fan
Meg is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl and her fan from earlier days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice girl' suggests the pop group; 'Spice' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of an evergreen tree is ground as a kitchen spice.
